note: All 55 official trophies with original guides. Counts appear only where the official description or the cited sources give a verified total.

trophies.guide: This is the platinum: it unlocks on its own once the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is nothing extra to grind for it directly. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then stranger strands, then counted activities, then collectibles — and keep an eye on the 14 flagged window-risk trophies, because a single missed one blocks this until a second run or an old save. Finish with A Long Road, then this pops automatically.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the game. It cannot be missed: playing the campaign from the start unlocks it as soon as that first mission ends. If you are replaying for a cleanup, there is nothing special to prepare — just start a new game and play through the introduction. Turn on the spoiler shield in this tracker if you want its name hidden until it pops.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Awarded when you finish every main mission of Chapter 1. It is unmissable on a normal playthrough — the chapter ends only through its final story mission. Before you close the chapter, consider doing the early meditation spots and meeting the first strangers, because Positive Mental Attitude is the one trophy sources flag as possibly tied to a Lucia meditation session in this chapter (unconfirmed).
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Unlocks at the end of Chapter 2 once its last main mission is done. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable if you keep following the story markers. A sensible habit from here on: finish any stranger strand you start before pushing the chapter forward, since the five named strand finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are flagged in this guide as window-risk because their descriptions tie them to a person's final mission.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Pops when Chapter 3 is completed through its final story mission. Nothing to prepare and nothing missable about the trophy itself. By this point most activity types should be open, so it is a good moment to tick off Master of None (try each of the 9 activity types once) and start banking stunts and races toward their counted totals while you travel between missions.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Earned by completing Chapter 4. Unmissable through normal story progression. After this chapter the endgame cleanup opens up: the collectible sets, the vehicle discovery count and the remaining counted activities are all far easier once the whole map and your contacts are available, so leave heavy farming for Stage 4 of the roadmap and keep the story moving.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: The story gold: finish the game's final mission and it unlocks. It is unmissable if you play the campaign to its end. Before starting the finale, make a separate save — several flagged trophies (Actions Speak Louder, Bad Luck, I Guess and Personal Best) have vague choice- or partner-based descriptions, and a pre-finale save is cheap insurance if any of them turns out to depend on an ending choice.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the named story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies like this one are unmissable: the mission sits on the main path and the trophy fires when it ends. If you skipped optional dialogue or failed an objective, replaying is not needed for the trophy itself — only completion counts. Keep the spoiler shield on if you do not want mission names shown ahead of time.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. It is part of the main campaign, so it cannot be missed on a full playthrough. Heists are also natural practice for Maximum Withdrawal (rob 5 bank vaults and escape): the same escape habits — change vehicle, break line of sight, then hide — carry straight over to the free-roam vault robberies you will farm later.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Unmissable: it is a required step in the campaign and the trophy unlocks at mission end regardless of how cleanly you played it. No preparation is needed; if a mission ever fails, simply retry it — only the successful completion matters for the trophy list.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners to earn this one. It sits on the main path, so a complete playthrough guarantees it. As with every named-mission trophy, medal quality and optional objectives do not matter — only finishing. This tracker hides its name behind the spoiler shield until you mark it earned, if you prefer going in blind.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. Unmissable on the main path. Note the separate trophy Catch Me If You Can also points at VCIA (an unscheduled departure there) and is flagged window-risk in this guide: while you are at VCIA for this mission, check whether the departure opportunity is available, because the description gives no second location for it.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. Like the other mission trophies it is unmissable and needs no special setup. Combat-heavy missions like this are a good place to practise Combat Focus, since Gunslinger asks you to take down 5 enemies in a single use of it — a dense firefight makes that far easier than open-world encounters.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the in-game checklist — the long gold of the list. Note the checklist asks for MORE than several trophies do: 300 stunts (trophy: 250), 30 race wins (trophy: 20) and 70 challenges (trophy: 50), while the meditation count differs the other way (checklist 15, GTABase reports 18 spots). Plan on the larger numbers everywhere and every counted trophy will pop along the way. Use the counter here to log your current percentage.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts anywhere in Leonida. The 100% checklist wants 300, so keep going past the trophy if you are chasing A Long Road. Stunts chain best on a fast bike around stunt jumps and ramps: repeat a short loop you can land reliably rather than touring the whole map. The counter in this tracker saves your running total and marks the trophy earned the moment you reach 250.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types at least once — winning is not required, participation is. The fastest route is to visit every activity icon that appears as the map opens up and start each one briefly. Because several other trophies (races, fishing, bowling, the range) live inside these activity types, doing this early also reveals where you will farm their counts later. Log each new type with the counter.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Work weapon by weapon and repeat a challenge until the gold threshold feels routine before moving on; accuracy challenges reward short bursts, timed ones reward memorising target order. There is no missable risk — the range stays available — so treat it as a late-game skill grind and use the counter to track how many golds you already hold.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location where the event is offered. The official description gives no total number of locations, so this guide deliberately shows no counter rather than inventing one — check the cited lists for the current location set before you start. Drone races reward smooth lines over raw speed: learn each course once at a safe pace, then push. Nothing here is missable; locations stay available.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the key word, so repeating one easy circuit does not advance the count. The 100% checklist asks for 30 wins, so keep racing after the trophy if A Long Road is your goal. A practical approach: sweep each race location once, note the ones you lose, and revisit those with a better vehicle. The counter here tracks distinct wins, not total starts.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the activity types, so this pairs naturally with Master of None: start the fishing activity, find Cal's challenge, and out-fish him. If you lose, retry — nothing in the description suggests a limited window, so treat it as a repeatable skill check. Patience on the reel timing matters more than the spot you choose.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game from start to finish. Find an arcade cabinet in the world, play a full game through to its end screen, and the trophy unlocks — a high score is not required, completion is. It is one of the quickest trophies on the list and a painless way to sample an activity type for Master of None at the same time.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's stranger strand. Work Andy's missions in order as they appear and do not shelve the last one: this guide flags every named strand finale as window-risk because the trophy is bound to that person's final mission, and strands are exactly the kind of content that can close when the story moves on. When Andy's last mission ends, the trophy pops and also counts toward the 8 strands of Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the description ties the trophy to Andy's final mission, so finish Andy's strand while it is offered instead of leaving its finale for post-story cleanup.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand through its final mission. Follow Kenton's markers whenever a new step appears and clear the strand in one stretch of play if you can. The flag here is precautionary, drawn from the description itself: a trophy tied to a named person's final mission is safest earned while that strand is active. It also advances Strangers & Freaks (8 completed strands).
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the trophy is bound to Kenton's final mission, so complete Kenton's strand promptly rather than postponing its finale.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's strand up to and including its final mission. Treat Billy like the other named strangers: start the strand when it appears, keep returning when new steps unlock, and finish the finale promptly. The description gives no alternative route, which is why this guide flags it — a missed finale would mean replaying to that point. Counts toward the 8 strands needed for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the trophy is bound to Billy's final mission, so do not leave Billy's strand unfinished while advancing the story.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The five named finales on this list — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — each count as one strand, so finishing all five puts you past halfway. Because this trophy depends on other flagged trophies, it inherits their window risk: clear strands as they open instead of batching them for the endgame. Track completed strands with the counter; it auto-earns at 8.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: it needs 8 completed stranger strands, and the five named strand finales are themselves flagged, so strands left unfinished are the risk here.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's stranger strand through its final mission. Same rule as the other named strands: play each step as it becomes available and do not let the finale sit while you push chapters. The flag is drawn from the description's wording — the trophy belongs to Randy's last mission specifically. Finishing it also counts as one of the 8 strands for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the trophy is bound to Randy's final mission, so finish Randy's strand while it is active.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand, including its final mission. Keep returning to Tyrone whenever the strand advances and clear the last mission as soon as it is offered. Like the other four named finales, this one is flagged because the description ties the trophy to that person's final mission — the safest reading is to finish strands while they are live. It also counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the trophy is bound to Tyrone's final mission, so complete Tyrone's strand promptly instead of deferring its finale.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida. Sources disagree on the total and this guide says so plainly: GTABase lists 18 spots, while the 100% checklist asks for 15 — work to 18 so both are covered. This is also the one trophy reported as possibly missable, linked to a Lucia meditation session in Chapter 1 (unconfirmed): meditate whenever a spot is available early on, and keep a Chapter 1 save as insurance.
trophies.missable_reason: Only trophy reported as possibly missable (GTABase/PowerPyx): it may be tied to a Lucia meditation session in Chapter 1 — unconfirmed, so meditate early and keep a Chapter 1 save.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Because the request comes from a named stranger, treat it like the strand finales: take Bret's hunt when it is offered and finish it in the same stretch of play. The description names no second chance or alternative animal, which is exactly why it carries a window-risk flag here. Bring a rifle you are comfortable with and approach quietly so the animal does not bolt.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the hunt is for Bret, a named stranger, so do it while Bret's strand is active rather than after moving on.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. Cards are a classic map-sweep collectible: pick one set, clear its locations region by region, then move to the next, and check the cited guides for the current card locations before sweeping. Nothing suggests cards expire, so this is safe endgame work. Use the counter to log finished sets — it marks the trophy earned at 3.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations across Leonida. This is a pure sweep: work district by district, tick off each location as you trigger it, and keep the counter in this tracker as your running total so you never re-check a finished area. There is no time pressure and no missable risk in the description. Pair the sweep with The Goodtime State (explore all of Leonida) to save travel.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. The 100% checklist raises the bar to 70, so if A Long Road is your target, plan for 70 and let this trophy pop on the way. Challenges accumulate naturally while you farm stunts, races and combat trophies, so check your challenge list before dedicated grinding — you may be closer than you think. The counter tracks your total and auto-earns at 50.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Reach a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the police and escape the heat together. Partner presence is the catch: the description requires your partner, and partner availability changes with the story, which is why this guide flags it. Build the stars somewhere with escape routes — water, tunnels, a pay-and-spray route — and break line of sight before hiding. Do it during a together stretch, not post-story alone.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: it needs your partner present at a 4-star wanted level, and partner availability follows the story, so attempt it while you are playing together.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.count_label: shops robbed in a row (with partner)
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner and never let the wanted level drop between them. Plan a tight cluster of shops, park a fast getaway car outside, and move shop to shop without hiding or changing clothes. Partner availability is the risk the flag points at: attempt it while the story has you together. The counter counts consecutive robberies in one run — reset it to zero if your wanted level clears early.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: it needs your partner beside you for 3 back-to-back shop robberies while keeping the wanted level, so it depends on partner availability.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Getting in and driving each new model you pass is the whole method: vary your districts, check parking lots, docks and airfields, and sit in anything unfamiliar. Vehicles also feed On the Spot (register 10 to the Scooter Bros app), so register finds as you go. The counter keeps your discovery total and marks the trophy earned at 100.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. The trick is density: trigger Combat Focus in the middle of a crowded firefight — a story shootout or a gang operation — rather than against scattered patrols. Line up targets before you activate so the whole window is spent shooting, not searching. Use the counter to record your best single-use tally; it earns at 5.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA. The description names one specific place, and VCIA is also where the story mission VCIA Takedown happens — that overlap is why this guide flags it: try the departure while you are there for the story, in case access changes afterwards. What counts as 'unscheduled' is not spelled out in the description, so check the cited guides for the exact method before attempting it.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the departure is at VCIA, a specific place the story also uses (VCIA Takedown), so try it while you have access to VCIA.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The official description — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — is a joke, not a set of steps, and this guide will not pretend otherwise. Rhinos are the game's tanks, so the trophy clearly involves one, but the exact trigger (stealing, destroying, surviving inside one) is not stated in the text. Check the cited sources for the confirmed method before you spend time hunting armor; this entry shows no counter because no verified total exists.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get away without being detected at all. Stealth is the whole trophy: case the store first, note staff and camera positions, and only move when nobody can see you. If you are spotted, leave and reset rather than forcing it — detection voids the attempt, not the trophy, so retries are free. Night visits and a quiet approach make the cleanest runs.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one — the escape is part of the count, so a vault you die leaving does not advance it. Stage a fast car and a change of clothes near each bank, hit the vault, then break line of sight before hiding. Rotate banks so you are not waiting on the same location. The counter only moves when you have both robbed and escaped; it earns at 5.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads, so watch for one while driving, block or ram it to force a stop, take the money, and lose the wanted level. As with the vault trophy, escaping is required — getting caught with the cash does not count. Keep a fast vehicle and a hiding spot in mind before you strike.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — every region of the map. The description gives no number of areas, so this guide shows no counter rather than guessing one; the in-game map shading is your progress meter. Sweep the edges and islands methodically, ideally while doing the WAiNK and card sweeps so the same travel covers three trophies. Nothing here can be missed; the map stays open.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. The description does not state how many gangs there are, so no counter is shown here — check the cited sources for the gang list and their operation locations before you start. Work gang by gang, and expect a fight at each operation: arrive armed, take the objective, and escape cleanly. These fights are also good Combat Focus practice for Gunslinger.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to Ocean Beach, find the bar or lounge spot overlooking the water, and order the cocktail — a one-step scenic trophy. It is available whenever you can reach Ocean Beach, so grab it the first time you pass through and cross it off. No combat, no timer, no missable risk.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style: get inside a showroom, take a display vehicle, and drive it out through the glass. 'Classic style' is doing quiet work in that description, so check the cited guides if a plain drive-out does not pop it — the exact flourish may matter. Expect a wanted level; have an escape route ready before you floor it.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and follow through — the description points at completing the bowling activity there rather than a specific score. Bowling is also one of the activity types, so a single game here advances Master of None as well. If the trophy does not pop on a casual game, check the cited sources for any score or strike requirement hidden behind 'follow-through'.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Honestly: 'A partnership with mass appeal' does not describe steps, and this guide will not invent them. The wording points at something you do with your partner that draws attention, which is why it is flagged — partner availability is story-dependent, so if it is tied to a together moment, post-story solo play might not offer it. Keep a rotating save, play partner activities when they appear, and check the cited sources for the confirmed trigger.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: the description is about a partnership, and partner availability follows the story, so watch for it while playing together.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Another honest entry: 'Choices made (for better or worse)' gives no count and no named choice, so no counter is shown and no steps are invented here. It plainly tracks decisions you make in the story, which is why it is flagged — a choice-based trophy can depend on options you have already passed. Keep manual saves before major story decisions, make choices deliberately, and check the cited sources for what actually triggers it.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: it is about choices made, and story choices cannot be unmade without reloading, so keep saves before big decisions.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' implies succeeding at something on a second attempt — but what, exactly, the description does not say, and this guide will not guess. The flag exists because a trophy built on a first failure may only be earnable in a specific sequence: if the first attempt is story-bound, a clean playthrough could pass it by. Keep saves, do not fear failing once, and check the cited sources for the confirmed situation.
trophies.missable_reason: Window-risk flag: 'Second time's the charm' implies a first attempt that can fail, and a failed first attempt may not be repeatable in the same playthrough.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: The description is a reaction — 'What the hell just happened?' — not instructions, so this guide states that plainly instead of inventing a location. It clearly marks witnessing something strange in the world. Random events and odd encounters are the natural hunting ground; if it does not pop during normal exploration, check the cited sources for the confirmed event and where it happens. No counter: no verified total exists.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by: lean out of a moving vehicle with a melee weapon and connect as you pass. Ride a motorcycle or sit in the passenger seat for the cleanest swing, pick a slow target on a quiet street, and time the swing as you draw level. A near miss costs nothing — circle back and try again. No window risk; it can be attempted any time you have a vehicle and a melee weapon.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and jobs; launder them steadily instead of hoarding, and keep a running total here — the counter earns the trophy at 250,000. This pairs with the robbery trophies (vaults, armored trucks, shops): every score both advances those counts and feeds this one. No missable risk; contacts stay available.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops combined — any shop counts, so ordinary spending on clothes, weapons, vehicle work and property upkeep all adds up. Late in the game, when money is plentiful, a deliberate shopping spree closes any remaining gap quickly. Track your spend with the counter; it marks the trophy earned at 100,000. Save this for after the big earners (heists, laundering) so it never strains your cash.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase every garage property in Leonida. The description gives no total number of garages, so this guide shows no counter rather than inventing one — the property listings in-game are your checklist, and the cited sources carry the current list. Garages are a money sink, so buy them late, after the heist and laundering income is banked. Nothing here expires; properties wait for your wallet.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Every vehicle you discover for Whip It Good (100 discoveries) is a candidate: when you find a new model, register it in the app before moving on, and this trophy finishes itself inside the first dozen finds. The counter tracks registrations and earns at 10. No missable risk — vehicles and the app remain available throughout.
trophies.name: On the Spot
